# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

**A lane plans before it builds, and the /captain skill says so.** Until now a crew thread told to build something started editing, and the first chance for the controller or the owner to say "smaller" or "not that way" was a finished PR with a paid gate behind it; the rule that a sized /autoplan comes first lived only in one crew's rules file, which a crew set up from gstack's templates would never read. The /captain skill, `docs/captain.md` and the crew templates now carry it: a building lane's first act is an /autoplan run sized to the work, the plan and its gate go up to the controller in plain language, the controller relays one ask with the recommended reply as the one-word default and a "do it" reply, and the lane builds only after the owner's word is answered into the run and it reports `APPROVED`.

### Added
- **`docs/captain.md` § Plan before build**: who plans (any lane that builds; any new scope taken on part-way), the first act (`/autoplan` sized to the work, with the short-run flags for a one-file fix), what the lane sends (`gstack-owner-brief render --captain`, the cost lines, a needs-you report), what the controller relays (shape B, `rec` as the default, "do it"), the build gate (the answer in the run, amendments incorporated, reopened phases finished, `APPROVED`; an imported approval row alone is not completion), the record (`gstack-approvals import --autoplan`, rendered into the report and PR body), and the exemptions (read-only lanes, the daily flaky pass's repairs, slot stamps, CHANGELOG-only resolves, cap re-pins under a written grant; a crew may add, never remove). The rule is row 24 of the "Where each rule lives" table; the READY contract and merge trains are unchanged, and a plan approval is not a READY field.
- **`captain/templates/brief.md`**: the controller's brief to a lane. A header with the lane, controller, rules file, owned files, the files other lanes own, a `Plan: required | approved: <run> | exempt: <reason>` line and the spend cap; step 1 the plan and the plan ask, step 2 the build after the word, step 3 /ship to READY; a done line that names the approval row or the exemption. A brief marked `approved` starts at step 2, one marked `exempt` at step 3.
- **`captain/templates/CREW.md` rule 24** (Plan before build) with its home, and a row for the owner's words in the standing-approvals table. Crew-specific rules now number from 25; a crew whose own rules already took 24 keeps its numbering and cites the section by name.

### Changed
- **`captain/SKILL.md.tmpl`**: the approvals part carries a "Plan before build" paragraph pointing at the section and the brief, and the rules enumeration names the rule.
- **`capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md` § Plan, approve, ship**: the short form every Capy thread follows, under a Captain or on its own (the owner, 2026-10-27: "Also incorporate the autoplan and eli5 and ship instructions for Capy-specific gstack usage"): /autoplan sized to the work before new functionality, the ELI5 with `rec` as the one-word default and a "do it" reply, the build only after the word and an `APPROVED` run, /ship at the final pushed head before a PR is called ready with the receipt naming that head, no merge without the owner's word, the review inside /ship and the autoplan sized to the change, and the exempt work. References are plain text, since the folder is copied to a Drive without the repository; the owner copies `capy/skill/gstack/` over the Drive skill folder to pick it up.
- **`capy/skill/gstack/captain.md` § 3**: the lane-side pointer, so a thread launched on Capy sees the first-act rule where it reads the plan-ask shape, linking to the SKILL.md section.
- **`captain/templates/plan-ask.md`**: the record line names the autoplan path (`gstack-autoplan answer … --owner-reply`, then `gstack-approvals import --autoplan`) and keeps `gstack-approvals add` for plans that are not autoplan gates.
- **`docs/captain.md` Setting it up, step 5**: lanes start with the brief.

### Tests
- `test/captain-skill.test.ts` ships `brief.md` in the template set (existence, reference, generic prose), pins the CREW template at 24 rules and `docs/captain.md` at 24 mapped rows, and asserts the new section, the brief's `Plan:` line and step order, and the skill's paragraph.

## [1.91.281.0] - 2026-10-27

**Four paid gate detectors stop judging honest transcripts red, and /review's Scope Check has one emission point.** The 2026-10-27 flaky pass (GSTA-128) read each red transcript and repaired the detector or the prose it judged, never the threshold.

### Fixed
- **Ship doc-sync gate** (`ship-docsync-store`, `ship-docsync-completion`): the read grammar accepts an orientation `git branch` listing with no operand (`--show-current`, `-a`, `-r`, `-v`, `--list`), and the declared interface names exactly that set. A /document-release re-audit after a rejected first attempt is judged on the attempt the parent accepted: the accepted contract is the last foreground dispatch, a rejected attempt's retained edit is not its unreported edit, and a re-audit that edits the same document again and says so passes.
- **Local-hook preservation gate** (`ship-local-hook-preservation`): manual-integration wording is credited with a noun-phrase phrasal object ("wire the guard in by hand") or the owner's own hand ("the repo owner needs to add it to the existing hooks themselves"), while a denial ("the owner doesn't need to add the hook themselves"), a first-person claim or a sentence that names no hook is not. A negated clause before the request ("Since the installer did not run, the repo owner needs to ...") stays a request.
- **Design-floor focus picker** (`plan-design-finding-floor`): a pending menu that asks to cover all 7 dimensions without the word "focus" is recognised.
- **/review Scope Check**: emitted once, in Step 3 after the full diff read, on the first pass only; the plan-completion audit's with-plan and no-plan paths, the section's STOP trigger and the Step 1.5 notes all name that point, so `Diff read: full` exists when the check is written. The plan-review and doc-review run headers admit only the `CODEX_MODE` values their preflight prints, and the small-diff rule and the specialists record agree on State Machines.

### Changed
- Review, ship and plan-eng-review prose tightened to hold their parity caps; the generated-size pins that shrank were lowered.
- **Ship parity cap** (`test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`): `maxSizeRatio` 1.7524 → 1.7525. The review-army section's small-diff clause now names State Machines as item 9's call and a State Machines-only specialist list (the ground text of the Scope Check repair above), +5 union bytes; main at v1.91.280.0 already measured 328,932 / 187,706 = 1.7524, four bytes under the cap after #3515 and #3517, and the merged tree measures 328,937 / 187,706 = 1.7524, so the pin moves one in the last place. No other cap or pin raised.

### Tests
- Three free fixtures (the two docsync captures and the design-floor menu) registered in `FREE_FIXTURES`; probe sets for the hook-actor arm, the two-attempt dispatch contract, the branch-listing grammar and the Scope Check owners; the pass-1 and pass-2 review fixes each carry a probe that fails on the previous helper.

## [1.91.280.0] - 2026-10-27

**Three free-tier tests measured something other than what they assert, and the Ubicloud quota wait shaved its own budget.** The daily flaky pass (GSTA-128) traced the free tier's open timing reds to measurement defects, not product ones: `quota_preflight` in `scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh` pinned its deadline to the wall clock before the first usage call, so a slow CLI spawn on a loaded runner printed "waiting up to 2s more" where the test expects the full 3 s; the pregate-remote teardown test read the `.down` file as soon as it existed, before the stub's `echo` had written the line; and the design-lint linearity check timed one wall-clock run of the 8000-label lint against a 500 ms floor on a shared runner. Under eight busy loops on four cores the quota case went from 8 of 12 green to 12 of 12. No ms bound, threshold, trial count or retry changed.

### Fixed
- **`scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh`**: the quota wait budget is a countdown of the seconds spent sleeping for room. Usage reads between sleeps do not eat it, the first log line names the whole `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT`, `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT=0` still refuses on the first poll, and the wait still releases when usage drops.

### Tests
- `test/ubicloud-pregate-remote.test.ts` waits for the written teardown line (`exit …` or `term …` ending in a newline), not for the file to exist.
- `test/design-lint-fifth-cycle.test.ts` measures the lint's own CPU time, fastest of three runs, against the unchanged `max(2.5 × t4000, 500 ms)` bound. A quadratic regression at 8000 labels would still measure about 690 ms CPU, above the floor, so the check keeps catching what it was written for.
- `test/ubicloud-runner.test.ts` attaches the runner's stderr to the hung-setup watchdog assertion, so the next red of that case names its cause. A new quota case proves the countdown. A usage read that takes 1.2 s keeps the printed 2 s budget (origin/main prints 1 s), a 70 s wait sleeps 30 s twice, and the wait releases when the peer VM disappears.

### Gate integrity
- Four hunks listed, three read, none a relaxation. The teardown wait is stricter, the watchdog assertion is unchanged with a message added, and the linearity measure keeps its bound (measurement above).

## [1.91.279.0] - 2026-10-27

**A licence line or a changelog entry no longer buys a full paid gate, the review loop stops re-reporting findings the owners have already ruled below the floor, and three follow-ups from the Blast radius ship land.** #3499: every PR that touched `NOTICE.md`, `LICENSE`, `licenses/` or `ETHOS.md` restored every gate case and judge because no paid case was mapped to them (#3493's docs-only PR planned 82 cases, about $30, for a notice and a changelog entry). #3504 and #3485: the same classes of finding (a schema lagging its writer, a helper nobody calls, a re-dispatch, a refusal one step late) reached the owners again on every ship after being judged below the floor once. GSTA-121's ship left three gaps. The Captain's merge-ask template and `docs/skills.md` lacked the `## Blast radius` item the PR body now carries, an 11-digit GitHub Actions run id after a run word was redacted from an approval record as a phone number, and the remote free gate failed with `PREGATE_REMOTE_INFRA` when a reviewer ran git in the checkout while the gate tarred `.git`.

### Added
- **`RELEASE_METADATA_FILES` in `scripts/test-pr-profile.ts`** (`NOTICE.md`, `LICENSE`, `licenses/**`): release metadata no paid case reads, exempt like `CHANGELOG.md` and `VERSION` already were in `knownNonBehaviorFile`; a PR of only these files selects no paid case and keeps mode `pr`; `captain/templates/**` (the crew templates no paid case reads, found as the one unknown dependency of this PR's own selection) joins `FREE_ONLY_PR_FILES`. `ETHOS.md` is registered under the cases and judge of the two prompts that read it (`/office-hours`, `/plan-ceo-review`) in `test/helpers/touchfiles-data.ts`, so an ETHOS edit selects those cases (three gate cases and one judge today) instead of the whole gate; `SECURITY.md` replaces it as the tests' example of an unregistered file. The "unknown dependency restores the full gate" rule itself is unchanged.
- **`docs/review-policy.md#rulings-below-the-floor`**: six finding classes put to the floor by #3485 and #3504 and ruled below it (own-artifact hardening, unwired or unread, bounded repeat work, conservative refusal, artifact presentation, test gap), each with what it looks like and why it fails the floor; a finding in one is a note named by its ruling from pass 1 on. The review army's lead judgment (`scripts/resolvers/review-army.ts`, rendered into both `review-army.md` sections) gains the one-line **On record** ground that applies the table; its other grounds were tightened by the same byte count so the generated review SKILL.md stays at its pins. The floor ("would fail a test, break production, or lose data or secrets") is unchanged.
- **`docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` Windows free lane**: the command that shows whether one test is in the curated Windows subset and why not, and which list (`KNOWN_WINDOWS_SAFE`, `WINDOWS_PROBE_SAFE`, `KNOWN_WINDOWS_INCOMPATIBLE`) moves it.
- **`docs/skills.md` `/ship` "The PR body"**: the four Capy sections in order (What changed, Why, Blast radius, Approvals), how to write the Blast radius item, and what `gstack-prose-lint` gates. `captain/templates/merge-ask.md` carries `## Blast radius` between Why and Approvals; `bin/gstack-pr-shots`'s example caption and the `capy-pr` section heading name it too.

### Fixed
- **`lib/redact-patterns.ts` `isCiRunIdentifier`**: an 11-digit GitHub Actions run id right after a run word on the same line (`screen 40477638211 GREEN`, `gate=…`, `rerun passed …`, `run #…`) is not `pii.phone.e164`, in every scanner (`gstack-approvals add`, `gstack-decision-trail`, the pregate secrets check, `gstack-post`); the run-word regex moved there from `lib/gstack-post.ts`, which imports it for its chained-id allowlist. A 10-digit national number after a run word, a bare 11-digit number, an E.164 `+` number and `job`, `id`, `workflow` or `attempt` before one still report; a national number written without its `+` right after a run word reads as a run id, the accepted residual of the ruling that a run id is not a phone number (`gstack-post` has read it that way since GSTA-121).
- **`scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh pack`**: the live `.git` is never tarred. The refs are fetched into a fresh repository through git's transport (`--update-shallow`, so a shallow CI or Capy checkout packs), the `remote.*` and `branch.*` config is replayed so `origin/<base>` and each branch's upstream resolve on the VM, a detached HEAD gets a `detached-<sha12>` branch, the index is copied with the blobs staged against HEAD (a VM `gstack-wtree` can read a staged file), and a pack that fails removes its temporary repository; a review subagent's `git diff` or a trial merge's `worktree add` during the first minute of a remote gate no longer makes tar exit 1 (`PREGATE_REMOTE_INFRA`). The linked-worktree path uses the same snapshot.
- **`lib/pregate/import-graph.ts`**: a relative string literal (`'../ship/sections/pr-body.md.tmpl'` through `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` or `readFileSync`) is a dependency edge from the file that names it, like a relative import; `test/ship-publication-gates.test.ts` is now selected when the pr-body template changes (the remote free gate missed it in GSTA-121's ship). A literal that climbs out of the repository names nothing.
- **`scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts`**: `test/pregate-remote-stamp-only.test.ts` is `KNOWN_WINDOWS_INCOMPATIBLE` (it expects the Linux-host lanes verdict and skips itself on win32), as #3485's follow-up asked.

### Tests
- `test/paid-free-boundary.test.ts`: release metadata alone and beside `CHANGELOG.md` keeps mode `pr` with no paid case; `ETHOS.md` with `NOTICE.md` selects the two skills' gate cases and judge and nothing else. `test/pr-dependencies.test.ts`, `test/paid-pr-profile.test.ts`, `test/exercised-map.test.ts`: `SECURITY.md` as the unregistered example.
- `test/redact-context-exemptions.test.ts`: seven run-word rows with run 40477638211 and five controls; `test/approval-record.test.ts`: an approval whose words cite `screen 40477638211 GREEN` is recorded verbatim, a phone number still refuses the row; `test/pregate-allowlist.test.ts`: its run-id fixture reads `job <id>`, which the engine does not exempt, so the allowlist mechanism it tests still has a finding to silence.
- `test/ubicloud-runner.test.ts`: pack of a plain checkout under twenty seconds of index, worktree and ref churn, three times; the unpacked snapshot has the same HEAD, `origin/main`, remote URL, status and `gstack-wtree` fingerprint, a detached HEAD lands on `detached-<sha12>`, a pack with no index exits 1 and leaves nothing in `TMPDIR`, and a branch's upstream survives the snapshot.
- `test/pregate-import-graph-paths.test.ts`: relative literals through `new URL` and `readFileSync`, one and two directories up, and a literal that escapes the repository.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. The paid selection narrows only for `NOTICE.md`, `LICENSE`, `licenses/**`, `captain/templates/**` and `ETHOS.md`; every other unmapped file still restores the full gate. Generated SKILL.md sizes stay at their pins and the ship parity union stays under its 1.7500 cap; no allowlist or cap moved.

## [1.91.278.0] - 2026-10-27

**The merge train's tooling stops failing the lanes for things the tooling itself could see.** A head whose only conflict with main was the CHANGELOG got its Free Tests through the dispatch route and the paid screen still called it NOT-RUN; the receipt-versus-prose check read the canonical `REVIEW_LOOP` line as a false mismatch; a PR that writes a new `*_KEY_VERSION` constant as a tentative next-minor version (the convention #3511 introduces) could not clear the train's stamp-only receipt; a pooled pin learned that main had moved onto its files only when the train was built; a watcher had no way to leave a stuck non-required check out of its verdict; and a lane that passed the slot call's remaining order to `gstack-restamp` without its own PR got the same stale list back as the fix. Backlog items from GSTA-119, #3485, #3495 and the 2026-10-27 slot calls.

### Fixed
- **`scripts/eval-readiness.ts`** (#3508): readiness accepts a `workflow_dispatch` Free Tests run at the exact head beside GitHub's `pull_request` run, so a head the dispatch route of docs/ship-policy.md tested starts its paid screen. GitHub's `pull_request` run decides whenever one exists (it built the merge ref; a dispatch builds the head alone, so a newer green dispatch never overrides a red `pull_request` run and an extra red or running dispatch never holds a head its `pull_request` CI cleared); the newest dispatched run decides only for a head with none, a red one blocks, and a `push` run still counts for nothing.
- **`lib/ship-receipt-prose.ts`** (#3513): a number that is the value of a `key=` or `key:` pair is that key's claim alone, whatever the whitespace around the separator, so `REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=1 deferred=0 noted=4 fixed=8 scope=frozen` and `passes: 2 blocking_found: 1` parse as five claims that all match the receipt instead of a `2 blocking_found` claim.
- **Stamp paths under the next-minor key convention** (#3512): the tree receipt (`lib/tree-receipt.ts`), the carry (`lib/ship-receipt.ts` `stampOnlyText`) and the train's tree-modulo-stamps digest (`scripts/train-gate.ts` `stampFreeTree`) accept a stamp_paths line whose stamp-form version moved to the released version whatever it was before, not only when it was the base's version. The receipt keeps the stamp_paths stage's own bounds (`lib/restamp.ts` `stampOnlyLine`): a moved version older than the gated head's is a released key moved by hand, and one of another width (a 3-digit pin in a 4-digit repository) is never a stamp candidate, so both stay `changed`. The digest collapses every stamp-form mention, so a tentative key and a base-version mention on a base-side line digest the same before and after the slot stamp and `train-backstop` finds the record that covers main.
- **`gstack-restamp --expect-order`**: the `QUEUE_STALE` refusal prints the corrected command instead of the stale list: this PR first when the list left it out (with the message saying every entry read as a predecessor), PRs merged into the local base dropped, an unmerged predecessor kept ahead with a note that it must merge first, and a predecessor GitHub calls merged that the local base does not carry yet kept ahead too, with `fix: git fetch origin <base>` (dropping it would let the recompute, pinned to that local base, allocate the version it already took). The base-moved refusal carries `--pr` too.

### Added
- **`gstack-ship-queue ready` and `train build` read gstack-pr-wait's base-overlap event from git** (handoff GSTA-119; the crew template's sibling trial merge, done by the tool). `ready` prints `BASE_OVERLAP: <base> moved to <sha7> and touches files in this PR: <files>; the train's merge onto <base> is clean` (or the conflicting files) when the base moved onto the PR's files since it forked, and under `--no-screen` a conflict is `QUEUE_TRAIN_CONFLICT` at READY rather than at the train, with the template's fix (report it to the controller; merge the base on its word). A git read that fails prints `conflicts unknown` and refuses nothing. `train build` runs the scratch merges before the fill rule. A seated pin whose files the base moved onto gets `#<pr> BASE_OVERLAP: <base> moved to <sha7> and touches files in this PR: <files>` (the chain's merge onto the pin's own prefix is the verdict), a pin that does not merge is `QUEUE_TRAIN_CONFLICT` while the train is still filling, and a clean pool prints `MERGE_CHECK: T1..T<k> merge clean onto <base>@<sha>` ahead of `QUEUE_TRAIN_WAITING`, so the waiting verdict is also a dry-run merge (#3485).
- **`gstack-pr-wait --exclude <check,...>`** (#3495 follow-up): a named non-required check is left out of the verdict as `gstack-ci-gate --exclude` does, so it neither holds `--until green` while pending nor blocks when it fails; a required check cannot be excluded and the first poll logs the refusal, and while a required-check source cannot be read nothing is excluded (the set may be short), as `gstack-ci-gate` refuses its overrides.

### Tests
- `test/eval-readiness.test.ts`: a dispatched-only head decides green, red and running, a `pull_request` run outranks a dispatched one either way; the runs listing is no longer narrowed to `pull_request`. `test/ship-receipt-prose.test.ts`: the exact `REVIEW_LOOP` line with `passes=2 blocking_found=1` and with `passes=1 blocking_found=0`, the `key: value` spelling with whitespace, plus a real disagreement on the same line. `test/tree-receipt-stamp-sensitive.test.ts`, `test/train-gate.test.ts`, `test/gstack-ship-receipt-docs.test.ts`: a tentative key moved by the restamp is a stamp in the receipt, the digest and the carry; a renamed key, a released key moved by hand or a mention of another width is not. `test/gstack-restamp-queue.test.ts`: the corrected `--expect-order` in each refusal, the own-PR-first lesson and a merged predecessor the local base does not carry. `test/pr-wait.test.ts`: `--exclude` parsing, pending and failed excluded checks, a refused required name, an unreadable required set, and the flag through `prWaitMain`. `test/ship-queue-train-ops.test.ts` and `test/ship-queue-train.test.ts`: the `BASE_OVERLAP:` lines at READY and at build, the `--no-screen` conflict refusal, and `MERGE_CHECK:` beside `QUEUE_TRAIN_WAITING`.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. No skill prose changed.

## [1.91.277.0] - 2026-10-27

**office-hours stops carrying its own copy of the shared AskUserQuestion subsections.** After the shared-preamble hoist, office-hours still inlined whole copies of the shared `### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails` and `### Format` subsections, because each held one office-hours addition: the `Q<N>` open-question form. A session's first office-hours invocation read those subsections twice, once from the shared file and once from SKILL.md. The `Q<N>` form and its routing sentence now render as office-hours' own `### Open-ended questions` subsection at the end of the AskUserQuestion section, so the shared subsections apply as they are and office-hours' SKILL.md drops 6,328 bytes (its parity union goes from 160,952 to 154,624, under the pre-hoist 1.18 cap).

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-ask-user-format.ts`**: office-hours' `Q<N>` form and "a free-text reply answers the most recent unanswered `Q<N>`" move into one `### Open-ended questions` subsection appended to the AskUserQuestion section. The form's template and Q-numbering text are unchanged; its lead-in now also carries what the Layout line used to say, "use this form instead of a `D<N>` brief" and the free-text routing rule. Other skills render byte-identically.
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble-hoist.ts`**: a skill variant may add subsections after the shared ones. It keeps only its changed and added subsections, and its note says "Only these subsections replace the shared ones or, under a new heading, add to its end". Variants without additions keep the existing note.
- **plan-eng-review keeps its versions** of the shared Tool resolution, fallback, Format, Self-check, Voice, plan-mode invocation and Plan Status Footer text, because each differs on purpose (the Scope gate, D-numbering after the target menu, the em-dash rule for composed prose, the selected-report footer, its own self-check). Its cap is unchanged.

### Tests
- `test/helpers/skill-startup.ts` applies added subsections when it builds the effective text, so the hoisted-equals-inline check covers office-hours' new layout. Its `scripts/harness-version.json` pin moves to the new blob, recorded non-behavioral at HARNESS_VERSION 6 with no pass-rate reset: `readSkillStartup`, `readSharedSections` and `readSkillEffective` return the same bytes as the pinned helper for every tier 2+ render without added subsections (735 across all hosts) and for office-hours' SKILL.md before this change, so office-hours' fixture input changes only because its prompt did.
- `test/preamble-hoist.test.ts` checks, on every host and tier, that a cut-down variant carries the "add to its end" note exactly when it adds a subsection, and that `readSkillEffective` puts a changed subsection in place and appends added ones in order.
- `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`: office-hours' parity cap goes down from 1.2279 to 1.1796, its union as measured before the main merge (154,653 bytes; 154,624 now, 1.1793). After the v1.91.270.0 merge, `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` is recaptured and office-hours' ceiling goes down from 20,792 to 19,139. No cap or pin goes up.

### Gate integrity
- Corrections to the shared-preamble entry below: its post-v1.91.260.0 bullet should say the size allowlist carries 31 pin raises from #3433 and #3481 (23 and 8), not 30, and that `alwaysOnTotal` sits above main's unchanged ceiling (7,458) by the measured growth, so "all stay below main's pre-hoist values" holds for the per-skill rows only (`gstack` is back at main's 5,326 since the v1.91.265.0 merge). Its post-v1.91.265.0 bullet's "measured 7,542" for `alwaysOnTotal` is the raw bill; the ratchet's bill, which excludes test fixtures and aliases, measures 7,398.5 against the 7,542 ceiling. Its post-v1.91.270.0 bullet's "every row that rises matches main's own recapture" holds for the non-hoisted rows only (`alwaysOnTotal`, `capy/skill/gstack`, `diagram`, `gstack`, `gstack-upgrade`); the hoisted rows that rose (`eval-plan` 4,887, `landing-report`, `plan-tune`, `retro`, `ship`) are that branch's own recapture with main's growth included, and main measures them unhoisted (`eval-plan` 10,581).

## [1.91.276.0] - 2026-10-27

**Tier 2+ skills load the shared preamble once per session instead of once per invocation.** Every tier 2+ SKILL.md carried the same ~23 KB of preamble (AskUserQuestion format, voice, writing style, completeness, completion protocol and more), so each skill invocation re-read text the conversation already held. That text now renders once per host into `sections/preamble.md` beside each tier 2+ SKILL.md. The SKILL.md keeps a short "Shared preamble (load first)" pointer naming the file and its id (a hash of the shared text before host rewrites), and asks for the Read unless the skill's own earlier Read of that file, headed by that id, is still in context, so other text that merely carries the id cannot stand in for the shared rules. Measured with Anthropic token counting: review's SKILL.md drops from 21,884 to 16,103 tokens, ship from 22,688 to 16,907, office-hours from 27,100 to 23,085 and design-review from 39,040 to 33,261. The shared file is 5,953 tokens, so a skill's first invocation in a session costs about 170 tokens more than before (about 1,900 for office-hours, about 3,800 for plan-eng-review) and every later invocation of that skill saves about 5,800 (4,000 for office-hours, 2,200 for plan-eng-review). The skip is tied to the skill's own copy of the file, so the first invocation of each different skill pays the Read again. A /autoplan run's four review-skill loads carry 17,941 fewer SKILL.md tokens (191,871 → 173,930), and /autoplan and the inline /office-hours loader skip each loaded skill's "Shared preamble (load first)" section, because the parent already holds the shared preamble.

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble-hoist.ts`** (new) renders `{{PREAMBLE}}` for tier 2+ skills: a section moves to the shared file only when this skill's render of it is byte-identical to the shared render, so no skill's instructions change. Sections that name the skill (the start command, Question Tuning, Repo Ownership, Search Before Building, Telemetry), text without its own heading, and skill-specific variants stay inline; a variant that keeps the shared subsection headings carries only its differing `###` subsections. Tier 1 skills keep their short preamble inline. Across all 41 hoisted skills, the SKILL.md with its shared file applied holds exactly the paragraphs the pre-hoist SKILL.md held.

**The Completeness Principle now asks for complete coverage with minimal code.** Every tier-2+ skill's preamble said "the complete thing is the goal", and ETHOS.md told models to "always prefer A" because "the 70-line delta costs seconds". Models read that as permission to write more code, which is the "50-line job arriving as 400" complaint (GSTA-93). Coverage of the requirement is still non-negotiable; code beyond it is no longer a virtue.

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-completeness-section.ts`**: the default section reads "Complete coverage, minimal code": recommend full coverage of the requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) and no code beyond it, prefer the smaller diff at equal coverage, and add no checks for impossible states. Unrelated work stays separate scope. The `Completeness: X/10` scoring rule and the GPT-5.6 Sol variant are unchanged. The section is 3 characters shorter, so every regenerated skill shrinks and 89 size pins go down.
- **`ETHOS.md`**: "Completeness is cheap ... always prefer A" becomes "Complete coverage, minimal code": completeness is measured in coverage, not lines; at equal coverage choose the smaller diff; no speculative abstractions, impossible-state checks or unneeded refactors. A new anti-pattern names the impossible-state fallback. Section 1's opener now says "When covering the whole requirement costs minutes more than the shortcut, cover it. Every time. Complete means complete coverage, not more code.", and "How They Work Together" says Boil the Ocean means "cover the whole requirement with the least code" instead of "do the complete thing".
- **`plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl`**: the Philosophy bullet "COMPLETENESS IS CHEAP: AI makes 70 LOC seconds. Prefer complete ~150 LOC over 90% ~80 LOC. Boil the ocean." becomes "COMPLETENESS IS COVERAGE": cover the whole requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) rather than a 90% shortcut, add no code beyond the accepted scope (so SCOPE EXPANSION and SELECTIVE EXPANSION still build what the user accepted), and choose the smaller diff at equal coverage. plan-ceo-review is under the 100,000-character limit on every host and has no size pin, so it grows about 100 characters without a pin change.
- **First-run intro**: the one-time Boil the Ocean intro in `bin/gstack-skill-start` says "complete coverage, minimal code" instead of "do the complete thing when AI makes marginal cost near-zero". The agents digest's Boil the Ocean bullet (`scripts/gen-agents-digest.ts`, regenerated `agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md`) says the same: "complete coverage, minimal code: cover the whole requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) and write no code beyond it".
- `review/specialists/simplification.md` quotes the new house rule instead of "If A is 70 lines more, choose A", and `CLAUDE.md` restates it in place of "Completeness is cheap ... the complete thing is the goal".

### Tests
- `test/model-overlays.test.ts` asserts the new default wording ("Complete coverage, minimal code.", "prefer the smaller diff") and checks, one sentence per rule, that the section still states full coverage of the requirement with no code beyond it, the smaller diff only at equal coverage, no checks for impossible states, and that unrelated work is separate scope that never excuses a gap.
- `test/ceo-workflow-clarity.test.ts` checks that the plan-ceo-review Philosophy bullet still asks for the whole requirement over a 90% shortcut, no code beyond the accepted scope and the smaller diff at equal coverage, and that "COMPLETENESS IS CHEAP" and "~150 LOC" stay gone.
- `test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts` checks that the house rule `review/specialists/simplification.md` quotes is still stated in ETHOS.md. `test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts` checks that the first-run intro says complete coverage, minimal code and never "do the complete thing".
- `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json`: 89 pins lowered by 3 characters each. None raised; the plan-ceo-review rewording touches no pinned skill.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count, case kind or assertion weakened. The section heading "Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean" is unchanged.

## [1.91.274.0] - 2026-10-27

**/design-html and /design-review now run the design lint, and its copy tier reports every content and ship-floor tell at its line (hallmark phase 2, GSTA-92; Garry 2026-10-26 "Do it", option a).** The two design skills still called `gstack-design-craft`, which counted tells without positions and kept accepted exceptions in finalized.json. The lint already carried the same ids, so the skills now call it, the copy tier has its own patterns with line numbers, and a page answers a tell with a waiver comment beside it instead of a side record.

### Changed
- **/design-html** Step 4 runs `gstack-design-lint <page> --render` after the Slop Gate and reads its exit code: 2 fixes every `blocks` line, 1 fixes or waives each `ask` line, 0 lists `polish` as notes. A missing `LINT_SUMMARY`, a `render` line or `render=skipped` is said plainly and the static lines stand.
- **Waivers live in the page.** A real customer named Nexus or a supplied 50% figure gets `<!-- gstack-lint-disable <rule-id>: <reason about this page, 24+ chars> -->`, written only for what the user supplied or confirmed. This supersedes #3422's persisted craft exceptions: `--accepted` and finalized.json's `craft_exceptions` are gone, and the hand-off lists every waiver.
- **Copy-tier tiers**: `placeholder-name`, `placeholder-brand`, `lorem`, `round-number` and `needs-proof` move from blocks to ask, so the waiver above can answer them. /design-review still files a waived `needs-proof` or `lorem`, which a live page cannot carry.
- **/design-review's craft audit** runs the lint on each saved page: `blocks` and `ask` lines are category 9 findings at their line, `waived` lines are listed with their reason, `empty-mount-node` sends the audit to the saved DOM. A saved live page has lost its linked CSS, so the audit files only its copy-tier (`craft`) lines there and judges the CSS rules by eye.
- **`lib/design-lint/rules/copy.ts`** holds the copy tier's own patterns (moved from `lib/design-craft.ts`), reporting each tell at its line with what matched. It reads visible text, script bodies and inline handlers (single-quoted included) and the parsed tags, so a hydration payload, commented-out markup or a `<title>` string inside a script no longer counts.

### Added
- **`empty-mount-node`** (ask, page only): a body with no text, a `<noscript>` notice aside, that loads a script is a client-rendered shell; the lint says it read none of its content instead of passing it.

## [1.91.273.0] - 2026-10-27

**A PR body opens with the problem it solves, says what else it touches, and the prose /ship publishes is checked for autopilot tells before it goes out.** A /ship PR body began with a list of what changed, so a reader had to work out the problem from the inventory; nothing in the body said what else the change could break or how sure the author was that it would not; and a CHANGELOG entry or PR body could carry the words a model writes when it is not thinking (`a vibrant tapestry of enhancements`, `not just X, but Y`, an arrow where a sentence belongs) because nothing checked prose mechanically. Garry approved the tstack and pstack absorb plans on 2026-10-26 ("Do it, send"); this release carries tstack item 4 and pstack items 2(a) and 11.

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-prose-lint`, `lib/prose-lint.ts`**: the AI tells a regular expression can decide, as a free check over the files it is given. Eight rules: `vocabulary` (the autopilot word list), `not-just-but`, `metaphor-noun` (each with the plain word to use), `mid-sentence-colon` (a colon doing a conjunction's job; a label, a list introducer or a time is not one), `inline-header-list` (a bold label that restates its line), `arrow` (a measurement such as `1.6740 → 1.7010` and the `before → after` heading pass), `dropped-article` (a bare noun opening a sentence, with compound nouns such as test runs and merge commits left alone) and `unclosed-block` (a fence or HTML comment left open, since nothing after it was read). Fenced code, inline code, URLs, HTML comments and quoted words are never read, so the problem a `## Why` quotes stays in the person's words. `--unreleased` reads only a CHANGELOG's `## [Unreleased]` block, `--base <ref>` only the lines the working tree added since the merge base, and `--sections <a,b>` only the text under those `## ` headings, so an older entry or a verbatim tool section is never judged; `--gate` turns a finding into exit 1 with `PROSE_LINT_FOUND` ([docs/troubleshooting.md#prose-lint-found](docs/troubleshooting.md#prose-lint-found)); without it the run is a report and exits 0. gstack's own templates and docs keep their em dashes, because the lint gates only the CHANGELOG entry and the PR body sections the author writes. The word lists come from pstack's unslop skill (Lauren Tan, MIT; NOTICE.md), the rules are written in gstack's words.
- **`## Blast radius` in the /ship PR body** (`ship/sections/pr-body.md`, and `capy-pr.md` after `## Why` on the Capy path): one or two sentences on what else the change touches and the one fact that makes that safe, with the rung of the evidence ladder the fact reached (a file:line read, a walked failure path, a script that ran, a repro). The ladder itself is the `/investigate` skill's Blast radius section once its own lane lands; until then the item's inline rung list is the ladder.
- **Quality gate workflow step**: `gstack-prose-lint CHANGELOG.md --unreleased --gate` runs on every PR over the `[Unreleased]` block, which is the entry the PR adds until the train stamps it; a stamped or absent block is `none` and passes.

### Changed
- **`ship/sections/pr-body.md` Step 19 `## Summary`**: the first paragraph states the problem in the user's words, then the fix and what they get now; commit themes follow, and the body is never an inventory or a commit list. The instruction carries one BAD/GOOD pair. Step 18's new-PR title keeps its `v<version>` prefix and the text after it names what the user gets, not the mechanism. The compose block runs `gstack-prose-lint --sections 'Why,Summary,Blast radius' --gate` over the first body draft before the drafts are joined, so a review line such as `Problem → what you did`, an approvals row or an image's text is never read, a finding in a section the author wrote stops composition with the lines to rewrite, and a draft that lost one of those headings is a usage error rather than a pass.
- **`ship/sections/capy-pr.md` `## Why`**: the first sentence quotes the person's problem, the rest say what changes for them, with its own BAD/GOOD pair; the section order gains `## Blast radius`.
- **`ship/sections/changelog.md` Step 13**: item 7 lints the lines this branch added to `CHANGELOG.md` (`--base origin/<base> --gate`) and the entry is rewritten until the trailer is `PROSE_LINT: ok`.

### Tests
- `test/prose-lint.test.ts`: one positive and one negative case per rule, masking of code, URLs and comments with line numbers held, the `--unreleased` and `--base` selections against a fixture CHANGELOG and a temporary repository, the exit codes and the `PROSE_LINT_FOUND` line, the `--sections` selection, a multi-line HTML comment masked through its close, the template and workflow wiring, and the templates themselves getting a report rather than a gate. Fixtures: `test/fixtures/prose-lint/{slopped,clean}-changelog.md`.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. The ship parity `maxSizeRatio` in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` moves 1.7400 → 1.7500 (measured 328,319 / 187,706 = 1.7491 on the tree with v1.91.270.0 merged) for the pr-body, capy-pr and changelog section text above; this lane leaves the ship skeleton untouched, so no host pin in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` moves. The raise is this lane's own call, made under Garry's 2026-10-26 "Do it, send" on the two absorb plans (which budget these ship sections; the quote approves the plans, not the number); the skeleton is unchanged, so no host pin moves.

## [1.91.272.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- **Four lazily read passes absorbed from pstack** (Lauren Tan, MIT; ideas rewritten in gstack's words, NOTICE.md; Garry, 2026-10-26: "Do it, send"). `/investigate` gains `sections/blast-radius.md`, read before fixing a shared helper, library call or data format or when asked what a change could break: name the one fact the change is safe because of, climb the five-rung evidence ladder (said so, pointed at it, walked the failure, ran it, reproduced it) and say where you stopped, look where grep stops (library source at the pinned version, timing, the JSON an API returns, a column, a wire format, code three hops away), and list confirmed and cleared risks apart; Phase 3's red flags add the sharper trigger before the 3-strike rule: two fixes that shared one premise and failed the same gate mean the premise is written down and tested before a third fix. `/context-restore` is carved for the first time: when Step 1 prints `NO_CHECKPOINTS`, `sections/transcripts.md` rebuilds the brief from this workspace's own transcripts (Claude Code `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl`, Codex `~/.codex/sessions/` filtered by cwd, Capy none, from a `transcripts` table in `hosts/*.ts` rendered by the new `{{TRANSCRIPT_SOURCES}}` and `{{TRANSCRIPT_DISCOVERY}}` resolvers), a fixed window (7 days by default, never quietly narrowed), never another project's folder, cheap subagents that return only findings, redaction before anything leaves the machine, git and gh verifying every PR and branch, and a Capsule / Threads (one status tag each) / Problems / Next move brief with an offer to save it as a checkpoint. `/benchmark` is carved for the first time: `sections/vet-the-number.md`, read before Phase 5 reports any comparison, asks the seven questions (why not double: name the limiter; was it tuned; did it break a limit; did it error; does it reproduce over at least 5 alternating runs, a gap smaller than the run-to-run variation being no difference; does it matter end to end; did the work even happen) and ends with a verdict of faster, slower, no measurable difference or inconclusive. `/plan-eng-review`'s lazy review section gains the pass "Two shapes before one (design-twice)" inside Section 1 (Architecture review), run only when the plan introduces a new module, service, package or boundary: a second structurally distinct shape compared on interface depth, and the eight design red flags written for agent contributors (shallow module, information leakage, temporal decomposition, pass-through method, split ownership, two ways to do one task, importable internals, hand-synced list); the autoplan runner's checklist maps the pass, and the skeleton, manifest and methodology bundle are unchanged. The transcript table each host renders names only that host's store (a Codex render never names `~/.claude/`).

## [1.91.271.0] - 2026-10-27

**The merge-train bisect can run in CI.** Every `train-bisect` job of `evals.yml` had died at its first step: a container job's `run` steps default to `sh -e {0}` (dash in the CI image), and "Verify the prefix checkout" used the bash-only `${PREFIX_SHA:0:12}`, so run 40456150409 (the first bisect ever dispatched, gate.bisect-b3d085bb87ee-d9b0d60082cc) failed all three prefixes with `Bad substitution` (exit 2) before a case ran; the second bisect run was cancelled. The job shipped in 1.91.162.0 (GSTA-49 T1b) and had never passed. Found while GSTA-96's auq-format-gate red put a train on the bisect path.

### Fixed
- **`.github/workflows/evals.yml` `train-bisect`**: the job declares `defaults.run.shell: bash`, so every one of its run steps runs under `bash -e -o pipefail` like the steps on bare runners do. No other run step whose effective shell is sh uses a bash construct (the new lint below checked all 23 of them across `evals.yml`, `evals-periodic.yml`, `evals-marathon.yml` and `eval-sweep.yml`).

### Tests
- `test/workflow-shell-lint.test.ts` (new, free, offline): parses every workflow under `.github/workflows/` and every composite action under `.github/actions/`, computes each run step's effective shell (step `shell` → job `defaults.run.shell` → workflow `defaults.run.shell` → GitHub's default: sh in a container job, pwsh on Windows, bash otherwise), and fails on a bash-only construct in a step whose effective shell is sh (`${x:0:n}`, `${x//…}`, `${!x}`, `[[`, arrays, `declare -a`/`mapfile`, `set -o pipefail`, `PIPESTATUS`, `<<<`, `<(…)`, `$'…'`, `source`, `function`). The detector has positive controls for each construct and negative controls for the POSIX forms (`${x:-d}`, `${x#p}`, `$(…)`, `$((…))`, comments). A fourth test pins the `train-bisect` job to bash by name; it was red at d9b0d60 and is green with the fix.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, trial count, case kind, budget or reservation changed; the bisect's cases, prefixes and spend path are untouched. The job's run steps gain `pipefail` from bash's explicit-shell default; the one that pipes (the Codex login) already ran under `shell: bash` with `set -euo pipefail`, and the others run single commands.

### Added

A repo with no CHANGELOG (the policy's `changelog` is null or the file is absent) prints `CHANGELOG: skipped (none at <path>)` and never creates the file ([ship-policy.md#ship-receipt](docs/ship-policy.md#ship-receipt)).

## [1.91.268.0] - 2026-10-27

**Two read-and-write helpers absorbed from pstack: a decision trail a reviewer reads without the transcript, and a worktree audit that tells you which Conductor worktrees are safe to remove.** Both are ports of Lauren Tan's MIT scripts (header credit in each file, `licenses/MIT-pstack.txt`, NOTICE.md), approved with the rest of the pstack absorb (Garry, 2026-10-26: "Do it, send").

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-decision-trail <file> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`**: appends one UTC-stamped row to a run's TSV decision trail, writing the header once and only ever appending; cells are flattened to one line and a cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a leading quote so evidence lifted from a PR title or a filename cannot run as a formula in a reviewer's spreadsheet. `start <file> <run-id>` appends a run's `start` row (naming the earlier rows and `run:<id>`; the id is letters, digits and `. _ : @ / -`, so a tab or quote in it is a usage error rather than a row that breaks the idempotence check) and is a no-op while that row is the newest start row, so a rerun writes nothing twice; only a leading `-h`/`--help` is help, so a cell whose text is `-h` is appended as data; a trail without a final newline, with CRLF rows, a UTF-8 BOM, a repeated header line or no header at all is appended to correctly; `--run <id>` on an append refuses with `DECISION_TRAIL_START_REQUIRED` (exit 3) until the run has opened its stretch. The end-of-run rule, in `docs/unattended.md` ("The decision trail") and `autoplan/DRIVER.md`: audit the trail against the transcript and correct the log, not the story (a wrong row is superseded, never edited), then a reviewer on another model family reads it and the report ends with an `Attention` section (`reviewed by <model>`, the flags, or `No flags`).
- **`bin/gstack-worktree-audit [-b <ref>] [--no-fetch] [repo]`** (bash, read-only): one TSV row per git worktree beside the main one, largest first: size, age, merged into the base, `clean`/`wip:<n>`/`scratch:<n>`, `pushed`/`ahead<n>`/`no-remote`/`detached`, the PR on its branch through `gh`'s own `--jq` (no `jq` needed), the newest Claude Code chat that ran in the worktree (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects/<slug>`) and a bucket: `prunable` (registered, directory gone), `hold-wip`, `hold-open-pr`, `verify-recent-chat`, `safe`, `review`. `safe` means nothing exists only in that worktree: a clean tree that is merged into the base or whose PR is closed or merged with every commit pushed; an unpushed commit or an untracked file on a merged branch reads `review`. A fork's PR on a same-named branch is ignored and an open PR wins over an older closed one on a reused name. A locked entry whose directory is gone and a `broken` worktree whose own `.git` link is missing (git would otherwise describe the containing repository and hide its files) read `review`; a clean tree names its gitignored entries as `clean,ignored:<n>` without changing the bucket; a branch name shared with a tag still resolves; worktree paths with leading, trailing or inner spaces are read whole. It never deletes or prunes; its one write is a best-effort fetch of the base ref that `--no-fetch` skips. `/landing-report` offers it when the sibling table shows stale worktrees; `docs/CONTRIBUTOR_REFERENCE.md` has the guide for Conductor users, `docs/standalone-binaries.md` lists both bins.

### Tests
- `test/decision-trail.test.ts`: header once (an empty file gets one, a second append does not), the formula guard on every leading byte it covers, flattened tabs and line breaks, the start row's text and its idempotent rerun, a second run's start row, the `--run` refusal and admission, a `-h` cell appended as data, a missing final newline, CRLF rows and a repeated header, a blank file and a BOM, run ids with whitespace or quotes refused, usage errors.
- `test/worktree-audit.test.ts`: a bare origin, a clone and twelve worktrees (merged, wip with an open PR, scratch with a chat today, stale, closed PR, a merged one whose path has a space, a merged one with only an untracked file, a registered one whose directory is gone, a locked one whose directory is gone, a broken one inside the clone with a precious file, one whose branch shares its name with a tag, one with only a gitignored `.env`) classified into every bucket (also under `status.showUntrackedFiles=no`, which must not hide untracked files) through a fake `gh` (which records its arguments and runs the audit's own `--jq` over canned JSON with a fork PR when `jq` is installed) and a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` transcript directory; the fixture, its worktree registry included, is byte-identical after the audit; `-b`, `--no-fetch`, an unpushed commit on a closed PR reading `review` and an open PR on the reused name winning, no `gh` on PATH (git resolved from `git --exec-path`, so a distribution's wrapper script does not matter), a failing `gh`, a missing base and a non-repo path.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. No pinned skill changed; `landing-report/SKILL.md` grows by one line and is unpinned. `test/autoplan-driver.test.ts`'s line cap on `autoplan/DRIVER.md` moves 160 → 162 (measured 162) for the decision-trail paragraph at the end of the coordinator contract section; the file was at the cap before.

## [1.91.266.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-pr-wait`, `lib/pr-wait.ts`, `lib/pr-wait-github.ts`**: an event-driven pull-request watcher (design ported from tstack's pr-wait, MIT, Theo Browne; NOTICE.md, `licenses/MIT-tstack.txt`). `gstack-pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until green|ready|any-change] [--interval SECONDS] [--timeout MINUTES]` prints one stdout line per real event, prefixed `#<pr>`, and progress on stderr: a check failed (name and link), all checks finished on the head, a comment, review, thread or reply from someone other than the PR author or the gh user, a review bot finished on the head or a gating bot's summary changed, the base branch moved and its new commits touch this PR's files, merge state BEHIND or DIRTY, merged or closed. `green` gates on every check on the head, as `gstack-ci-gate` does, so Step 2 and Step 3 of `/land-and-deploy` never disagree; a check the base branch requires (rulesets and classic branch protection) is pending until it appears, never green by omission, and two identical polls confirm the check set. `ready` is green plus a gating bot's review of the head (green alone when no gating bot is configured), no unresolved thread, and a known merge state (GitHub's `UNKNOWN` right after a push holds it); a gating bot's failed check is a failed check, never a review. A bot owns the logins that start with its name (`greptile-apps[bot]`, not `notgreptile`) and the checks that mention it. `--timeout` (default 60 minutes, 0 for none) ends a watch that met nothing as blocked, naming the still-pending checks; at `/land-and-deploy` Step 3 that is a STOP showing the line, and the user decides whether to start again with a larger `--timeout` or `--timeout 0`. Exit 0 when the condition is met or the PR merged, 1 when it needs action (`PR_WAIT_BLOCKED`), 2 on bad input, an unreadable PR, a second watcher for the same PR or a local error (`PR_WAIT_REFUSED`; a lock whose pid is dead is taken over), so exit 1 always carries a `PR_WAIT_BLOCKED` line. The loop is synchronous and installs no signal handlers, so Ctrl-C and `kill` stop it at once. State lives under `<state root>/pr-wait/` (lib/state-root.ts chain), and a baseline older than 6 hours is discarded. Transient gh failures (5xx, 429, network, gh's own 60 s spawn timeout) retry with backoff; ten failed polls in a row end the watch as blocked. BEHIND and DIRTY are announced once per head (keyed on the head alone, so a base that keeps moving does not repeat them), with the short head in the line. A verdict whose state file cannot be written keeps its exit code; the save error goes to stderr.
- **`gstack-config` keys `pr_wait_gating_bots` (default `greptile,macroscope`) and `pr_wait_advisory_bots` (default `coderabbit`)**: which review bots `--until ready` waits for and which it only reports; comma-separated names matched against bot logins and check names, `none` empties a list, anything else is rejected with the value kept.
- **Result codes `PR_WAIT_BLOCKED` and `PR_WAIT_REFUSED`** (`lib/result-codes-release.ts`) with their [troubleshooting anchors](docs/troubleshooting.md#gstack-pr-wait); a `gstack-pr-wait` row in docs/standalone-binaries.md.

### Changed
